source_text: Nam si Lex Dei fons est ac magistra iustitiae, auxiliis quoque eius, Dei aequitas adiuvari potest, impugnari non potest. Nullum ergo adminiculum iniquitati de illius Scripturae viribus comparari natura rerum sinit, quae hanc unam promulgationis causam habuit, ut eius testimoniis, remediis, minis, ultionibus iniquitas deleretur.
pass_a_gloss: For if the Law of God is the fountain and mistress of justice, by its helps also the equity of God can be aided, it cannot be attacked. Therefore the nature of things allows no prop for iniquity to be got from the strengths of that Scripture which had this one cause of promulgation, that by its testimonies, remedies, threats, vengeances, iniquity should be destroyed.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: For if God's Law is the source and teacher of justice, its support can uphold God's fairness; it cannot attack it. The nature of things therefore does not permit injustice to draw any support from the authority of that Scripture whose sole reason for being proclaimed was to destroy injustice through its testimonies, remedies, threats, and punishments.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
